## ✅ Implementation complete — Bookmark Manager

All 32 tasks done; **39 automated tests pass** (31 unit/API + 8 Playwright end-to-end covering every quickstart scenario), plus a manual smoke test confirming the API, static UI, and persistence across restart.

### What was built (against the approved spec/plan)
A single Node.js + Express app serving both the UI and a JSON API, backed by a local SQLite file.

| Area | Files |
|------|-------|
| Server + API routes | `src/server.js` |
| Data access & business rules | `src/bookmarks.js` |
| Storage/schema | `src/db.js` |
| URL validate/normalise/dedupe | `src/url.js` |
| Best-effort title fetch | `src/title-fetch.js` |
| Browser UI | `public/index.html`, `public/app.js`, `public/styles.css` |
| Tests | `tests/unit/`, `tests/api/`, `tests/e2e/` |

### User stories delivered
- **US1 Save** — validates/normalises the address (`example.com` → `https://example.com/`), auto-fetches the title when blank, warns on duplicates (with "save anyway").
- **US2 Browse & open** — newest-first list, opens in a new tab, empty state.
- **US3 Edit & delete** — edit form + delete with a required confirmation.
- **US4 Search & tags** — live search over title/address/notes/tags, tag filter, clearable no-results state.

### Two fidelity fixes made during implementation (spec unchanged)
Both were implementation defects caught by the tests, so I fixed the code against the spec rather than changing the spec:
1. Non-http schemes (`ftp:`, `javascript:`) now rejected with the correct message.
2. Timestamps keep millisecond precision so quick edits update `updated_at` correctly.

### Ready for your review
The harness is configured (`/work/.harness/app.json`, `npm start`, port 4000). The broker will launch it on demand — you'll reach it at **http://maker:4000**. The UI signals readiness via `data-harness-ready="true"` once the list/empty state loads.

Would you like to review it in the browser, or shall I adjust anything? If you spot behaviour you'd like changed, tell me which — I'll route it either as a fidelity fix (code only) or, if it's a spec change, back through `speckit-specify` and re-plan as our workflow requires.
